Fit the backward joint model to interval-censored event times

Source: R/imputeEventTime.R
fitIntervalBJM.Rd

Experimental. With interval censoring nobody's event time \(T\) is known exactly – only \(L < T \le R\) – so the longitudinal sub-model \(f(Y \mid T)\), which has \(T\) as a covariate, cannot be fit on the subjects with an observed event the way it is for right-censored data. fitIntervalBJM() fills in \(T\) by stochastic EM, then by multiple imputation:

  1. fit the marginal survival model to the intervals (survivalSub() with Surv(L, R, type = "interval2")); it does not depend on \(T\), so it is fit once;

  2. start every interval-censored \(T\) at its interval midpoint and fit longitudinalSub();

  3. draw each subject's \(T\) from \(f(T \mid L < T \le R, Y, X) \propto f(Y \mid T, X) f(T \mid X)\) on \((L, R]\) (imputeEventTime()), refit longitudinalSub(), and repeat for n_burnin iterations;

  4. keep iterating, saving every n_thin-th draw and its longitudinalSub() fit until n_imputations are saved.

Step 3 uses the backward model's own factorization: \(f(Y \mid T)\) on a grid of \(T\) is exactly what dynamic prediction already computes (conditionalYT()), so each draw costs about one predictRisk() call per subject.

By default only subjects whose event was observed (finite \(R\)) enter the longitudinal fit, mirroring the complete-case fit used for right-censored data, which is valid when censoring is independent of \((T, Y)\) given the covariates. include_right_censored = TRUE also imputes \(T \in (L, \infty)\) for right-censored subjects and uses them; their draws then rely on the survival model's extrapolated tail.

The saved draws come from one chain, so successive draws are correlated; saving only every n_thin-th iteration makes them closer to independent. They are drawn with the model parameters at their point estimates, not from their posterior, so the between-imputation variance in pooled can still be somewhat understated.

For prediction, long_fit_all combines the imputations: its fixed effects are the Rubin's-rules pooled estimates and its residual and random-effects variances the averages over the imputations (see poolLongitudinalSub), so a prediction does not depend on which single imputation happened to come first. With competing risks the event-type model of survival_fit_all likewise has its coefficients averaged over the imputations.

Usage

fitIntervalBJM(
  data_survival,
  data_fit_all,
  form_marginal_surv,
  event_time,
  long_sub_fixed,
  long_sub_random,
  time_variable,
  survival_variable_all = NULL,
  survival_trans_function = NULL,
  form_conditional_cr = NULL,
  n_burnin = 10,
  n_imputations = 5,
  n_thin = 5,
  n_grid = 40,
  baseline = c("spline", "piecewise"),
  df = NULL,
  include_right_censored = FALSE,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

data_survival

One row per subject: the interval endpoints, the survival covariates and the subject id.

data_fit_all

As in longitudinalSub: one data frame per biomarker (or one shared data frame), long format, for every subject. The event_time column and the columns named in survival_variable_all are (re)filled from the imputed \(T\).

form_marginal_surv

Surv(L, R, type = "interval2") ~ covariates.

event_time

Name of the event-time column used in long_sub_fixed.

long_sub_fixed, long_sub_random

As in longitudinalSub.

time_variable

Name of the visit-time column.

survival_variable_all, survival_trans_function

Transformed event-time columns, as in predictRisk (NULL if none).

form_conditional_cr

Optional competing-risks (event-type) model, as in survivalSub, e.g. type ~ Tev + x. The event type (0/1, in data_survival and in every data_fit_all data frame, alongside the covariates of this formula) is taken as known once the event is detected; each subject's \(T\) is then drawn from \(f(Y \mid T, D) P(D \mid T) f(T)\), and this model, which uses \(T\), is refit on every draw.

n_burnin

Stochastic-EM iterations before draws are saved.

n_imputations

Number of saved draws (and longitudinal fits).

n_thin

Iterations between saved draws (1 saves every iteration after the burn-in). Larger values make the saved draws less correlated at the cost of n_burnin + n_imputations * n_thin iterations in all.

n_grid

Grid points per subject interval.

baseline, df

Baseline hazard of the survival model (see survivalSub).

include_right_censored

See Description.

seed

Optional integer seed (the global RNG state is restored).

Value

An object of class "fitIntervalBJM", a list with survival_fit_all (with competing risks, its event-type model has the coefficients averaged over the imputations, while the rest of that glm object, e.g. its standard errors, is the first imputation's fit; survival_fit_all_list has one fit per imputation); long_fit_all_list (one longitudinalSub() fit per imputation); long_fit_all (the imputations combined, see Description, for use with predictRisk() and friends); pooled (poolLongitudinalSub of the fits, when n_imputations > 1); imputed_T (a subjects x imputations matrix); and trace (each iteration's fixed effects, to check the chain has settled).
